c.tagline: Morocco's northern gateway — a whitewashed medina above the Strait of Gibraltar.

taxi.fareNote: Blue petits taxis handle short in-city hops (make sure the meter is on, or agree a price, before setting off) while cream grands taxis run fixed shared routes; app-based Careem has only a limited presence, so street taxis are the norm.

emergency.note: Dial 19 for police and 15 for ambulance/fire; 112 also works from mobile phones. Tourist police patrol the medina and main sights.

avoid.reason: Hustlers and fake guides at the port and medina; caution at night

hood_desc: The walled old town of narrow whitewashed lanes tumbling toward the port, packed with souks, riads, the Petit Socco cafes, and craft workshops. Best for atmosphere and first-time visitors.

The fortified hilltop quarter crowning the medina, with the Kasbah Museum (Dar el Makhzen), panoramic ramparts over the Strait, and boutique riads in restored palaces. Suits those after views and quiet charm.
The French- and Spanish-era new town around Place de France and Boulevard Pasteur, with cafes, the Terrasse des Paresseux viewpoint, banks, and modern shops. A convenient central base.
The seafront strip east of the port along the bay, lined with modern hotels, a beach promenade, and resorts stretching toward Cap Malabata. Good for beach stays and sea views.
A leafy residential plateau west of the Kasbah with early-20th-century villas, the clifftop Café Hafa overlooking the sea, and a calm local feel. Suits a quieter, authentic stay.

water.note: City tap water is chlorinated but most visitors stick to bottled.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 9-10 PM; blue petits taxis operate day and night and fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Tangier has no metro or tram. Alsa runs the modern city bus network, but most visitors rely on cheap blue petits taxis for short hops and cream grands taxis for longer shared runs. The medina and Kasbah are walk-only.
transit.pay: Pay bus fares in cash on board; petits taxis are metered (insist on the meter) and paid in cash — carry small dirham notes and coins.

bus: CTM & Supratours intercity coaches from the bus station
ferry: Fast ferries to Tarifa, Spain (Tangier Ville port, ~1 hr)
Car ferries from Tangier Med to Algeciras & Barcelona, Spain
train: ONCF Al Boraq high-speed to Rabat & Casablanca; conventional trains to Fez & Marrakech from Tangier Ville station

transit.m: Airport bus to the train station via the city centre (~40 min, fixed 40 MAD fare)
Grand taxi to city centre (fixed government tariff, ~20-25 min)

tip.r: ~5-10% at restaurants; small change (a few dirhams) for cafe waiters, porters and guides is expected.
